summary: This article explains how puppeteers use hand puppets, string puppets, and shadow puppets to make lifeless objects seem alive, and how puppetry traditions have told stories across many cultures for centuries.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “Puppetry: Telling Stories with Objects”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: a puppet moved by strings held above it
a custom or way of doing something passed down over many years
a show put on in front of an audience

challengeTerms.def: something that looks real or true but is not
customs, art, and traditions passed down from earlier generations
to control or move something skillfully with your hands

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a puppet show can tell a story just as well as actors can? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how puppetry traditions are similar across the places described in the article.
struggling: Pre-teach marionette, tradition, and performance with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses illusion, heritage, and manipulate to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
